## This steering file was generated by Kiro based conditions established throughout our conversation history.

# Project Conventions

Standing rules Kiro should follow in this repository. A steering file with
`inclusion: always` is loaded into every chat automatically, so these do not
need to be restated each session.

## Platform
- Development happens on Windows using PowerShell. Use PowerShell command
  syntax (e.g. `Get-ChildItem`, `;` as the command separator, `$env:VAR`),
  never bash-only syntax.

## Repository layout
- Python code and data live under `backend/`:
  - `backend/marciano_json_to_df.py` — flattens one menu JSON into a per-item
    DataFrame.
  - `backend/collect_menu_dfs.py` — recursively combines every menu JSON under
    `backend/data/<date>/menu_*.json` into one item-level DataFrame.
  - `backend/dining_diet_analysis.py` — builds the per-dining-hall summary.
  - `backend/data/<YYYY-MM-DD>/` — one folder per service day, each with
    `locations.json` and `menu_<hall>.json` files.
- Paths are anchored with `Path(__file__)` so they survive moves and run on any
  machine. Do not reintroduce hard-coded absolute paths.

## How to run the pipeline
Run (or import) the modules in this order; each depends on the previous one:
1. `marciano_json_to_df.py`
2. `collect_menu_dfs.py`
3. `dining_diet_analysis.py`

In Jupyter, restart the kernel (or `importlib.reload`) after editing a module,
because Python caches already-imported modules and will otherwise run stale code.

## Data-handling rules
- Missing item text (most often `description`) is stored as the literal string
  `"null"`, never a float `NaN`. Numeric and boolean columns keep real
  `NaN`/`<NA>` so averages and shares stay correct.
- The feed provides only four nutrition fields: `calories`,
  `carbohydrates_grams`, `protein_grams`, `saturated_fat_grams`. There are no
  vitamins or minerals; do not invent nutrition columns the data lacks.
- Discovery of menus is recursive and data-driven. Never hard-code dining hall
  names; process whatever the data / `locations` response contains.

## Analysis conventions (domain definitions)
- Entrée vs component: separate real meal options from condiments, dressings,
  breads, sweets and drinks, so counts are not inflated by trivially-suitable
  ingredients (e.g. plain olive oil being vegan). The station lists are
  editable as the station vocabulary grows.
- Treat every dietary need equally: `vegetarian`, `vegan`, `gluten_free`,
  `halal`, and `cool_food` (climate-friendly) each receive the same set of
  metrics, generated in a loop. Do not over-emphasize any single diet.
- Column names must be plain English and self-describing (e.g. `percent_vegan`,
  not `pct_vegan`). Percentages are on a 0–100 scale.

## Working style
- Validate every change by actually running it and checking concrete outputs
  before reporting success. A clean exit is not proof of correctness.
- Read the real data and files before writing code against them; do not assume
  structure.
